subject: Best Way to Override Default Theme?

messages.author: da498f62395fbbd6
messages.subject: Best Way to Override Default Theme?
parts:
Hello All,

I have recently upgraded to ggplot2 v2.2. The default alignment for plot titles has changed in this version from Centered to Left Justified.

I am aware that I can add a "theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))" clause to my ggplot/qplot statements to cause the title to be centered, but I have hundreds of scripts and thousands of ggplot/qplot statements that I now need to remediate. I really do not want to have to add the additional plot.title clause to every ggplot statement.

I am hoping there might be some statement(s) I could insert at the beginning of each script, or include in my .RProfile, to cause all plot titles to be centered.

I believe that I am using the default theme_grey, but also have many ggplot statements that include ... + theme_bw() + ...

I have tried adding the statement at the top of my script, before any plotting:

theme_bw <- theme_bw() %+replace% theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

but that seems to have no effect.

Any help appreciated.

Thanks,
Champ Lee

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Best Way to Override Default Theme?
parts:
I think you're trying to create a custom theme. There's no reason you can't do what you're doing, but I think you shouldn't override an existing theme like that to avoid collision issues later. 

Emulate the source of a custom theme like the following at the top of your file:
https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/master/R/theme-defaults.r
https://github.com/hrbrmstr/hrbrthemes/blob/master/R/theme-ipsum.r

Something like:

theme_champ <- function(base_size = 11, base_family = "") {
  # Starts with theme_bw and then modify some parts
  theme_bw(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) %+replace%
theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "red"))
}


Then you just use it: 
library(ggplot2)

#needs a title to change
ggplot(mtcars, aes(cyl, disp)) + geom_point() + labs(title = "MakeATitle") +theme_champ()


HTH,
B

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: Re: Best Way to Override Default Theme?
parts:
Champ Lee is looking for theme_set(). Start each script with the lines below and the default theme will be theme_champ() instead of theme_grey().

library(ggplot2)

theme_champ <- function(base_size = 11, base_family = "") {
  # Starts with theme_bw and then modify some parts
  theme_bw(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) %+replace%
theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "red"))
}

theme_set(theme_champ())

Best regards,
